eva: FYI I'm seeing weird quality drops after we switched phi-2.1 to int8 for the cheapest bucket. small but reproducible on instruction-following tests.
sam: Thanks, what's the metric delta?
eva: On the eval harness: pass@1 down ~3.2% and answer hallucination increased on QA prompts. Not huge but consistent across seeds.
michael: Any perf wins though? int8 should be ~1.7x throughput.
eva: Latency is fine for small batches, throughput up ~1.6x. But memory looks jittery on longer contexts (>=2048). saw multiple allocation failures in the logs.
ana: can you paste the error?
eva: ```
[2026-03-19T14:12:03Z] runtime: allocation failed: device OOM, attempted 3.2GB
[2026-03-19T14:12:03Z] trace: kv_cache_alloc failed, frag_high=0.78, free_blocks=12
```
sam: kv_cache_alloc + fragmentation. we saw similar with other quantized configs when the KV chunking didn't line up.
michael: Did the kernel selector pick the int8 fused GEMM path? that can change transient peak working set.
eva: It picked `int8_fused_qgmm` on A100s. I forced `int8_fp16_kern` and memory spikes dropped, but quality still off.
ana: Could this be quantization-induced accuracy regression (scale/bias mismatch) rather than perf? Have we tried per-channel calibration vs symmetric global?
eva: Good call. I ran a small sweep: global symmetric vs per-channel asymmetric on the feed-forward gave per-channel a 2.4% improvement back towards fp16. Still ~0.8% off.
michael: That's within expected for aggressive 8-bit, but we can tighten by using mixed-quant: int8 for MLP, int16 for attention weights. Tradeoff in perf ~8-12% slower than pure int8.
eva: Tried mixed: quality matches fp16 within noise, throughput drops to ~1.35x.
sam: For production, maybe we keep int8 in cheaper tier but pin a slightly smaller default `max_new_tokens` for long-context workloads to avoid the fragmentation scenario?
eva: I'm also seeing that our default `max_new_tokens=256` plus `batch_size=12` causes the runtime to hold many partial KV buffers which amplifies fragmentation. If we reduce `max_new_tokens` to 128 for phi-2.1 int8 policy, OOMs disappear in tests.
ana: Does that affect user-visible behavior? short tasks unaffected, but generative apps might hit truncation. We can add model-specific route that sets `max_new_tokens` default and expose override.
michael: Also enable periodic GC/compaction on session tear-down: `runtime --compact-kv on-evict` reduced free_blocks from 12 -> 42 in my run.
eva: Config changes I propose: 1) phi-2.1 int8 policy: default max_new_tokens=128, max_batch_size=8, enable kv compaction on evict; 2) mixed-quant promoted to dedicated tier; 3) add per-channel quant calibration in our quant pipeline.
sam: Sounds reasonable. Can you open a short PR with config and a note in the model onboarding doc? Also add a small eval comparing fp16/int8/mixed on our `instruct-200` suite.
eva: Will do. PR + eval run queued.
ci-bot: Build queued: model-configs/phi-2.1/int8-defaults -> CI#4521.
infra-bot: Canary deploy scheduled to `dedicated-eu` with traffic split 95/5 in 30m.
ana: For the record, let's track a regression ticket for hallucination delta as well. if int8 still shows residual gap we should consider a light finetune on instruction data before shipping.
michael: I can prototype a 1-epoch lo-fi fine-tune on 10k examples to see if we can recover that last 0.8%. low cost.
eva: Awesome. I'll attach the eval results to the PR when CI finishes. thanks all :raised_hands:
